questions.q: Name the two major gaseous pollutants released during combustion of coal in a thermal power plant that contribute to acid rain.
questions.a: Sulphur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ). A wrong answer (e.g., naming CO₂ or CO) reveals the student confuses greenhouse gases with acid rain precursors — a specific board exam trap where SO₂/NOₓ are the required keywords for acid rain questions.

questions.q: Explain why nuclear energy is considered a low-carbon source but still poses a long-term environmental hazard that fossil fuels do not.
questions.a: Nuclear fission emits negligible CO₂ during operation (low-carbon), but produces high-level radioactive waste (spent fuel) requiring isolation for thousands of years — a persistent radiological hazard absent in fossil fuel waste. A wrong answer focusing only on "radiation leaks" or "meltdowns" misses the specific distinction: **routine waste management** vs **accidental release**, which is the board exam differentiator.

questions.q: A 500 MW coal-fired power plant operates at 35% efficiency. Calorific value of coal = 25 MJ/kg. Carbon content = 70% by mass. Calculate the mass of CO₂ emitted per hour. (Molar mass: C=12, O=16). Use the reaction: C + O₂ → CO₂.
questions.a:
**Step 1:** Electrical energy output per hour = 500 MW × 3600 s = 1.8×10⁹ J = 1800 MJ.  
**Step 2:** Heat input required = Output / Efficiency = 1800 MJ / 0.35 = 5142.86 MJ.  
**Step 3:** Mass of coal burnt = Heat input / Calorific value = 5142.86 MJ / 25 MJ/kg = 205.71 kg.  
**Step 4:** Mass of carbon in coal = 70% of 205.71 kg = 144 kg.  
**Step 5:** Moles of carbon = 144,000 g / 12 g/mol = 12,000 mol.  
**Step 6:** Moles of CO₂ produced = 12,000 mol (1:1 stoichiometry). Mass of CO₂ = 12,000 mol × 44 g/mol = 528,000 g = **528 kg CO₂ per hour**.  
A wrong answer often forgets the efficiency factor (Step 2) or uses 12 g/mol for CO₂ molar mass — both are common board exam calculation errors.

questions.q: Compare the environmental impact of a large hydroelectric dam versus a solar photovoltaic farm of equivalent capacity (100 MW) on three parameters: (i) land submergence, (ii) methane emissions, (iii) end-of-life waste.
questions.a:
(i) Hydro: submerges vast forest/agricultural land (ecosystem loss, displacement). Solar: uses dry/waste land, no submergence.  
(ii) Hydro: submerged vegetation decays anaerobically → significant CH₄ (potent GHG). Solar: negligible operational emissions.  
(iii) Hydro: minimal waste (concrete/steel). Solar: panels contain toxic metals (Cd, Pb) requiring e-waste recycling after 25 years.  
A wrong answer claiming "hydro has zero emissions" ignores reservoir methane — a specific IPCC/NCERT highlighted issue.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Biogas plants solve both energy and waste problems in villages with zero negative environmental impact."
questions.a: **False.** While biogas utilizes cattle dung/agri-waste (reducing methane from open decay) and provides clean cooking fuel, it has impacts: (1) Slurry discharge can cause waterlogging and nitrate leaching if not managed. (2) Incomplete combustion in traditional stoves still emits particulates. (3) Large-scale plants may compete with fodder/fertilizer use of dung. Board exams test this nuance: **renewable ≠ impact-free**.

questions.q: Design a simple school-based investigation to compare particulate matter (PM2.5) levels near a diesel generator set versus a rooftop solar installation during operational hours.
questions.a: **Good answer criteria:** (1) Use identical low-cost PM sensors (e.g., Plantower PMS5003) placed 5m from each source at same height. (2) Log data every 5 min for 2 hours during typical load. (3) Control: measure background AQI simultaneously. (4) Present as time-series graph with mean±SD. (5) Conclude with statistical comparison (t-test if taught). A poor answer lacks controls, uses single snapshot readings, or ignores meteorological variables (wind).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: ______ consequences of energy sources refer to the detrimental effects on air, water, soil, and ecosystems resulting from the extraction, conversion, and utilization of energy resources, including greenhouse gas emissions, particulate pollution, radioactive waste, habitat destruction, and thermal pollution.
Fill in the blank: Observe the thick smog over Delhi in winter or the ash pond near a local thermal power plant — these are visible ______ of burning coal.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can systematically compare the environmental footprint of fossil fuels, nuclear, solar, wind, hydro, and biomass sources across parameters (CO₂ emissions, land use, waste, water impact) and justify which source is most sustainable for a given Indian geographical context.
